title: Las murallas
goal: Hear why this quarter is called Xalteva
culture: Xalteva was the indigenous town, and the Spanish built their city beside it rather than on it. The low walls along the street are what is left of the boundary between the two, and people walk past them every day without knowing that is what they are.

beats.es: ¿Ve esa pared baja? Eso no es de ahora, joven.
beats.en: Did the indigenous people live here?
beats.good: Los indios is the ordinary word here and carries no sting in this sentence. He will use it himself and so does the history he is about to give you.

beats.es: Aquí era el pueblo de ellos. Xalteva se llamaba, antes de que llegaran los españoles.
beats.good: Antes de puts a date on something without needing one, which is how this history is told: before the Spanish, before the earthquake, before the war.

beats.es: Antes. Y los españoles levantaron su ciudad al lado, y una muralla en medio.
beats.good: La muralla divided the two towns. What is standing is a fraction of it and nobody has signposted a metre of it.

beats.es: Un pedazo. Es lo que queda, joven. Lo demás se lo llevaron para hacer casas.
beats.say: Lo que queda. Gracias por contarme.
beats.en: What’s left. Thank you for telling me.
ok: lo que queda gracias por contarme
beats.good: Lo que queda — what is left. Thanking him for the telling rather than for the wall is the difference between a tourist and a neighbour.
